case_title: Ram Autar & Ors. v. State of U.P.
previous_criminal_record: No. The evidence showed the appellants had no infamous criminal background.
accused_victim_relationship: Neighbour (accused resided next door); distant relative (descended from a common ancestor, grandfathers were real brothers); prior dispute over cattle trespass and crop damage.
statutory_provisions: IPC s.302 (charged, with ss.147/149; s.148 against one accused); finally convicted under IPC s.304 Part I read with ss.147, 148, 149
evidence_type: Eyewitness testimony; medical (post-mortem); forensic (blood-stained earth and chemical analyst report); sketch map of scene
aggravating_circumstances: Joint lethal attack by several accused using a firearm and lathis; the prosecution alleged an exhortation by a co-accused to eliminate the deceased.
mitigating_circumstances: Sudden quarrel on the spur of the moment; deceased contributed to escalating tension; no prior criminal record; incident occurred in 1982, more than three decades earlier.
trial_court_outcome: Convicted under ss.302, 147, 148 and 149 IPC; life imprisonment for s.302 IPC and other sentences.
high_court_outcome: Conviction under ss.147/148/149 upheld; s.302 conviction altered to s.304 Part I; sentenced to 10 years rigorous imprisonment and Rs.5000 fine (default two months simple imprisonment).
offence_finally_established: IPC s.304 Part I read with ss.147, 148 and 149
neutral_facts: The victim's cattle allegedly strayed into the fields of neighbouring residents in the morning and damaged a standing crop. The neighbours abused the victim, who drove the cattle back home. In the early afternoon, the victim was sitting in his compound with his brother, a second witness and a third witness, when a dispute broke out between him and neighbours who lived next door over the same issue. The exchanges grew heated and the neighbours, including the accused, allegedly closed in on the victim. On being urged by another neighbour to eliminate the victim, one of the accused allegedly fetched a gun and fired at the victim, who fell injured. The other accused then allegedly struck him with sticks. The victim's brother and two witnesses who tried to intervene were allegedly stopped by the gun being pointed at them. The victim died at the spot. The first information report was lodged at about 3.15 p.m. the same day. Investigation included an inquest, a sketch map of the scene, and collection of blood-stained earth, which a chemical analyst found to be human blood. Three eyewitnesses testified to the sequence of events and identified the accused. The post-mortem doctor recorded firearm wounds on the head, chest and right upper arm, multiple abrasions and contusions, and death from shock and haemorrhage. The doctor also recorded simple lacerated or incised wounds and contusions on some of the accused. The defence contended that the accused had been attacked while escorting cattle and that one of them fired in self-defence.
physical_harm: Death of the victim from firearm wounds to head, chest and right upper arm, with multiple abrasions and contusions; death due to shock and haemorrhage.
number_of_offences: 4 charged (ss.302, 147, 148, 149 IPC); 4 finally upheld (s.304 Part I, ss.147, 148, 149 IPC)
premeditation_planning: Court found no premeditation or prior concert; the incident arose on the spur of the moment.
motive: Dispute arising from the victim's cattle trespassing into the accused's fields and damaging the crop, escalating into an afternoon altercation (the Court found no common object to eliminate the deceased).
key_evidence_accepted: Eyewitness testimony of PW-1, PW-2 and PW-4; post-mortem evidence of PW-5; sketch map and blood-stained earth with chemical analyst report corroborating the place of occurrence; rejection of the self-inflicted-injury defence explanation.
witness_credibility: Eyewitnesses found consistent and cohesive, identified the accused and gave detailed sequential accounts; concurrent findings of the courts below accepted.
trial_duration: offence: 04.04.1982; trial judgment: not given; High Court: 10.06.2016; Supreme Court: 28.11.2016
legal_representation: Accused: Dr. J. P. Dhanda, Ms. Raj Rani Dhanda, Vineet Dhanda, N. A. Usmani, Mohd. Shahid Hussain. State: Ravi Prakash Mehrotra, V. S. Shukla, Vibhu Tiwari.
investigation_status: FIR registered at about 3.15 p.m.; inquest and sketch map completed; charge-sheet filed; charge framed; trial completed.
appeal_history: Trial court: convicted under ss.302, 147, 148, 149 IPC (life for s.302). High Court: ss.147/148/149 upheld; s.302 altered to s.304 Part I; 10 years RI. Supreme Court: appeal partly allowed; sentence under s.304 Part I reduced to 7 years RI.
prosecution_argument: Eyewitness testimony proved the accused formed an unlawful assembly, intending to eliminate the deceased, and jointly launched a lethal attack including a firearm; conviction should not be interfered with and the sentence was lenient.
defence_argument: Accused were attacked while escorting the cattle and one fired in self-defence; no premeditation or pre-concert; the High Court sentence was unduly harsh and should be scaled down.
legal_principle_applied: Absence of premeditation, prior concert or common object to kill; sudden quarrel on the spur of the moment with loss of self-control, supporting culpable homicide (s.304 Part I) rather than murder; contribution of the deceased to escalation considered.
sentencing_rationale: Singular facts and circumstances: sudden quarrel, no premeditation, no criminal background, and more than three decades since the 1982 incident.
judicial_mitigating_factors: Spur-of-the-moment incident with loss of self-control; deceased obdurately refused to withdraw and contributed to escalation; no infamous criminal background; over three decades elapsed since 1982.
other_sentence_order: Trial Court directed to take necessary follow-up steps to ensure the appellants serve the sentence; other sentences affirmed.
